 Sharvari Wagh Brings Pastel Elegance To The Great Indian Kapil Show In Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla
 Sharvari Wagh brings pastel elegance to The Great Indian Kapil Show in a sage green anarkali by Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla. Featuring intricate antique gold embroidery and a flowing silhouette, the ensemble offers a fresh take on Indian occasionwear. Take a closer look at her outfit and styling details
 By
 Sonali Mukherjee 
 13 November 2026 11:59 AM
 Sharvari Wagh makes a case for pastel Indian couture in a sage green anarkali by Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla. The actor shared photographs of the ensemble on Instagram ahead of her appearance on The Great Indian Kapil Show, where she joins Ayushmann Khurrana and the cast of her upcoming film, Yeh Prem Mol Liya. The look combines traditional craftsmanship with a softer colour palette, offering an elegant reference for festive and celebratory dressing.
 Sage green gives the ensemble a distinct identity without relying on a bright shade. It also provides a subtle backdrop for the antique gold embroidery, which lends the outfit its ornate character. The combination brings together the richness of Indian couture and the appeal of understated colours.
 Sage Green Anarkali Brings Pastel Elegance 
 Sharvari’s latest look centres on a sage green anarkali featuring intricate antique gold embroidery. The fitted bodice follows an empire-waist construction before opening into a floor-length, flared skirt. This proportion defines the upper silhouette while allowing the skirt to fall freely. A deep scoop neckline adds shape to the bodice, while the scooped back introduces a contemporary detail to the traditional design.
 The embroidery is central to the Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla outfit. Set against the muted green base, the antique gold detailing creates contrast and gives the ensemble its festive finish. The design draws its visual interest from the interplay of the soft base shade, metallic work and sweeping silhouette.
 Also Read: An Evening At The Unveiling Of Grey Goose Altius X Amit Aggarwal’s Cocktail Couture 
 Anarkalis remain a familiar choice for festive gatherings and wedding occasions because they combine the structure of a fitted bodice with the ease of a flared skirt. Here, the restrained colour palette gives the traditional form a contemporary direction. It offers an option for those who enjoy Indian occasionwear but prefer softer shades to brighter festive colours.
 Antique Gold Accents Complete Ethnic Look 
 Sharvari’s choice of antique gold jewellery complements the embroidery, keeping the accessories in harmony with the outfit. The metallic accents add definition while allowing the craftsmanship and silhouette to remain the focus.
 When a garment features intricate surface detailing, accessories in a complementary finish can bring the look together without making it appear overworked. Sharvari’s appearance illustrates how coordinated jewellery can give traditional Indian attire a polished finish.
 Her ethnic look also offers inspiration for those exploring pastel occasionwear. Sage green provides an alternative to conventional festive shades, while antique gold detailing retains the richness associated with celebratory dressing. The combination works particularly well for wedding functions , intimate festivities and daytime occasions where softer colours can make an impression.
 Appearance On The Great Indian Kapil Show 
 Sharvari shared glimpses of her appearance on The Great Indian Kapil Show through Instagram, accompanying the photographs with a playful caption about sharing laughter, enjoying the family atmosphere and finding another reason to dance. She joined Ayushmann Khurrana and the cast of Yeh Prem Mol Liya for the episode.
 Also Read: H&M Beauty Names Sharvari Its First India Ambassador 
 The episode is scheduled to stream on Netflix on November 14, at 8 pm. The appearance comes ahead of the theatrical release of Yeh Prem Mol Liya on November 27. Directed by Sooraj Barjatya, the film brings together an ensemble cast for a family entertainer.
 Her latest ethnic fashion look brings together three enduring elements of Indian occasionwear, i.e., the anarkali silhouette, intricate embroidery and a considered colour palette. Her choice of sage green offers a fresh alternative to brighter festive shades, while the antique gold detailing preserves the richness of traditional Indian couture.
